fields.category: Penn State peach varieties for Pennsylvania home orchards

rows.name: Candor
rows.description: First early peach of the season with any quality. Fruit are yellow and medium in size, but a large percentage tend to produce split seeds, limiting usefulness for canning

rows.name: Harrow Diamond
rows.description: Medium to medium-large fruit with attractive scarlet-red skin over a greenish-yellow ground color. Fruit is semiclingstone

rows.name: Garnet Beauty
rows.description: Good early peach ripening just before Redhaven. Source describes it as semiclingstone to freestone, very productive, and medium sized

rows.name: Glenglo
rows.description: Yellow-fleshed peach that is attractive, medium large, moderately firm, semifreestone, and low in susceptibility to bacterial spot

rows.name: Reliance
rows.description: New Hampshire peach with better-than-average bud hardiness. Source says fruit quality is only fair, but this is the only variety to try on marginal Pennsylvania peach sites

rows.name: Redhaven
rows.harvest_time: Aug 1 in southcentral Pennsylvania; Aug 8 in central Pennsylvania
rows.description: Standard and most popular peach variety in the industry. Fruit quality is good; fruit size may be small if not properly thinned. Source says freezing quality is above average and canning quality is below average

rows.name: Harbrite
rows.description: Agriculture Canada Harrow Station release. Productive freestone with medium to large round fruit, good winter hardiness, and reported resistance to bacterial spot and brown rot

rows.name: Redkist
rows.description: Medium to medium-large peach with crimson-red skin. Fruit is firm and freestone. Tree has low susceptibility to bacterial spot

rows.name: Beekman
rows.description: Red sport of Sunhigh found in an orchard in Boyertown, Pennsylvania. Fruit is very firm and high quality, with showy large flowers

rows.name: Harmony
rows.description: Productive winter-hardy peach with medium to large fruit that freezes well. Source notes it is sometimes listed in nursery catalogs as Canadian Harmony

rows.name: Madison
rows.description: Firm-fleshed high-quality peach good for freezing. Trees are more tolerant to frost than other varieties and are recommended in northern areas of Pennsylvania

rows.name: Cresthaven
rows.description: Medium to large nearly round peach, very uniform, golden with abundant bright red overlay. Yellow-fleshed freestone with considerable red around the pit

rows.name: Encore
rows.description: Large firm freestone peach with 60 to 70 percent crimson-red skin over greenish-yellow ground color

fields.category: Penn State nectarine varieties for Pennsylvania home orchards

rows.name: Harflame
rows.description: Medium dark red-skinned nectarine with yellow ground color. Fruit are semifreestone, with somewhat acidic but very good flavor

rows.name: Harblaze
rows.description: Medium to large nectarine with bright-red skin over orange-yellow ground color. Fruit are semiclingstone

rows.name: Crimson Snow
rows.description: New white-fleshed nectarine with pinkish overcolor and slight greenish ground color. Source says fruit may be small and needs heavy thinning

rows.name: Fantasia
rows.description: Large yellow-fleshed nectarine that is firm, highly colored, and good quality. Tree is somewhat susceptible to bacterial spot

rows.name: Redgold
rows.description: Good late-maturing freestone nectarine with red-over-yellow skin and yellow flesh with red around the pit. Source notes susceptibility to bacterial spot

fields.category: Penn State plum varieties for Pennsylvania home orchards

rows.name: Methley
rows.description: Early ripening Japanese plum of good quality and appearance. Fruit are round, sweet, very juicy, and purple with red blush. Flowers are partially self-fruitful, but Shiro or Ozark Premier can increase yield

rows.name: Shiro
rows.description: Round yellow Japanese plum with occasional pink blush. Source notes the fruit are clingstone but very juicy

rows.name: Castleton
rows.description: Cornell dual-purpose prune/plum. Fruit is blue, round, and similar to Stanley

rows.name: Ozark Premier
rows.description: Large bright-red Japanese-type plum with tough skin, yellow juicy flesh, fair quality, tart flavor tendency, clingstone fruit, and small seed. Source says it will not pollinate Stanley or Bluefre

rows.name: Bluebyrd
rows.description: European type plum from the USDA station in Kearneysville, West Virginia. Fruit is firm and sweet with yellow flesh

rows.name: Seneca
rows.description: Cornell release with large reddish blue fruit and excellent dessert quality. Fruit is reported resistant to cracking and brown rot

rows.name: Stanley
rows.description: Medium dark-blue freestone European plum, oval with a distinctive neck. Well suited for processing and drying, with greenish-yellow juicy fine-grained flesh

rows.name: Long John
rows.description: Cornell European type producing large long teardrop-shaped blue freestone fruit

rows.name: Bluefre
rows.description: European type producing large blue yellow-fleshed freestone fruit. Fruit hangs well on the tree but produces many split pits

fields.category: Penn State disease-resistant plum candidates for Pennsylvania home orchards

rows.name: AU AMBER
rows.description: Auburn disease-resistant plum candidate with medium-sized purple-skinned fruit and excellent flavor. Fruit is smaller than AU Rosa and AU Rubrum. Partially self-fruitful

rows.name: AU ROSA
rows.description: Auburn disease-resistant plum candidate with bright-red skin and yellow flesh

rows.name: AU RUBRUM
rows.description: Auburn disease-resistant plum candidate with large firm fruit, maroon skin, and red flesh. Reported to be self-fruitful

rows.name: AU CHERRY
rows.description: Auburn disease-resistant plum candidate described by Penn State as a small plum that has consistently produced large crops

rows.name: AU ROADSIDE
rows.description: Auburn disease-resistant plum candidate with red-skinned fruit and high-quality flesh. Flowers are self-fruitful

fields.category: Penn State apricot varieties for Pennsylvania home orchards

rows.name: Harcot
rows.harvest_time: First week in July in southcentral Pennsylvania
rows.description: Canadian introduction that has been a consistent producer when not frosted out. Needs thinning for acceptable size. Fruit is attractive with red blush, good early-season fresh quality, and unsuitable canning quality. Reports from New York indicate resistance to brown rot and bacterial spot

rows.name: Veecot
rows.description: Medium to large round apricot with very firm deep-orange fruit. Flesh is smooth textured, slightly juicy, and cans well

rows.name: Hargrand
rows.description: Harrow, Ontario apricot with glossy fruit averaging 50 percent orange-red surface blush. Fruit is somewhat flattened with mild good flavor. Reports from New York indicate resistance to brown rot and bacterial spot

rows.name: Harogem
rows.description: Medium-sized apricot with bright-red glossy blush over orange background. Tree growth is very upright and trees are very resistant to cold. Reports from New York indicate resistance to brown rot

rows.name: Harlayne
rows.harvest_time: Third to fourth week in July
rows.description: Bright-red blushed apricot, often small and requiring careful thinning. Source says fruit is best suited for fresh eating and reports from New York indicate resistance to brown rot and bacterial spot

fields.category: Penn State tart cherry varieties for Pennsylvania home orchards

rows.name: JUBILEUM
rows.description: New tart cherry developed in Hungary. Fruit are very large with dark red flesh, not as tart as Montmorency, and have very high sugar levels

rows.name: Danube
rows.description: Popular European variety with dark red fruit slightly sweeter than Montmorency. Fruit are medium to large, and trees may be a little less winter hardy than Montmorency

rows.name: Montmorency
rows.harvest_time: Last week of June to first week of July
rows.description: Number one tart cherry variety and industry standard. Productive, but flowers are susceptible to late spring frosts

rows.name: Surefire
rows.description: Recent Cornell introduction. Late-blooming tart cherry that can avoid spring frost damage. Fruit is bright red and medium in size

rows.name: Balaton
rows.description: New late-maturing tart cherry with large very firm fruit and red burgundy juicy flesh

rows.name: NORTHSTAR
rows.description: Dark-juiced cherry with mahogany-red medium-sized fruit. Trees are very hardy and small, making them easier to net against birds

rows.name: Meteor
rows.description: Medium-sized semifirm good-quality fruit. Trees are somewhat larger than North Star and equally hardy. Source notes the oddly shaped pit can shatter during processing, which is not a problem for home use

fields.category: Penn State sweet cherry varieties for Pennsylvania home orchards

rows.name: Vista
rows.description: Nearly black excellent-quality sweet cherry fruit, about 7/8 inch in size. Source lists it as self-unfertile and needing a compatible pollen source

rows.name: Ulster
rows.description: New York introduction with medium-sized firm dark-skinned dark-fleshed fruit. Source lists it as self-unfertile and needing a compatible pollen source

rows.name: Viva
rows.description: Vineland Research Station release with dark red fruit about 3/4 inch in diameter. Source lists it as self-unfertile and needing a compatible pollen source

rows.name: Hartland
rows.description: Early-season crack-resistant black cherry. Tree is vigorous, crops consistently, and is self-unfertile according to the source

rows.name: Royalton
rows.description: New York Agricultural Experiment Station release with large dark sweet cherries, high sugar levels, and some crack resistance. Source says it is cross-compatible with Emperor Francis, Kristin, Sam, Schmidt, and Ulster

rows.name: Emperor Francis
rows.description: Large high-quality Napoleon-type cherry less subject to cracking. Fruit can be used for brining or fresh use and has attractive red blush over yellowish background

rows.name: Sam
rows.description: Early ripening large black sweet cherry. Tree is large, vigorous, upright, and later blooming than most sweets. Fruit has good resistance to rain-induced cracking. Source notes Sam is pollen incompatible with Royalton and Schmidt

rows.name: Kristin
rows.harvest_time: Last week in June in southcentral Pennsylvania
rows.description: Norwegian introduction with one-inch fruit of good quality, good flavor, high sugar content, and moderate rain-cracking resistance. Source notes pollen incompatibility with Somerset and Group I cherries

rows.name: Viscount
rows.description: Canadian 1983 introduction producing medium-large firm good-quality dark glossy-red cherries. Productive and has good crack resistance

rows.name: Hedelfingen
rows.description: Medium-large firm good-quality black cherry with moderate cracking resistance. Trees are early bearing and very productive

fields.category: Penn State self-fertile sweet cherry varieties for Pennsylvania home orchards

rows.name: Vandalay
rows.description: Self-fertile sweet cherry with large wine-red kidney-shaped fruit and purple juice. Developed in Vineland, Canada

rows.name: Stella
rows.description: Self-fertile sweet cherry with large dark-red fruit. Trees are productive but can be tender in cold winters, so source does not recommend it for more northern Pennsylvania areas

rows.name: Tehranivee
rows.description: Mid-season self-fertile sweet cherry developed in Ontario, Canada. Source notes cracking can be a problem

rows.name: SONATA
rows.description: British Columbia 1996 introduction with very large black moderately sweet fruit

rows.name: WHITEGOLDTM
rows.description: Cornell early mid-season self-fertile sweet cherry selection for processing, used similarly to Napoleon or Royal Anne, with considerable potential for brining and processing markets

rows.name: Symphony
rows.description: British Columbia 1997 introduction with bright-red very large fruit that matures late in the season. Source says it has shown better rain-cracking resistance than other varieties from this program

rows.name: BLACKGOLDTM
rows.description: Cornell late mid-season self-fertile sweet cherry selection. Latest-blooming sweet cherry in the Cornell collection with remarkable tolerance to spring frost. Primary use is fresh eating

rows.name: Sunburst
rows.description: British Columbia 1983 introduction. Fruit is large and firm, and trees are productive

rows.name: Lapins
rows.description: Summerland Research Center release with Stella as one parent, making it self-fertile. Fruit is very large and somewhat crack resistant

rows.name: Skeena
rows.description: Very large dark mahogany cherry. Source says it is superior to Lapins, has unknown cracking susceptibility, and blooms in mid-season

rows.name: Sweetheart
rows.description: High-quality British Columbia sweet cherry with very large late-maturing fruit. Trees are productive, yielding dark-red medium to large firm fruit with good flavor
